name: Open-Faced Tuna Nicoise Sandwich (Pan Bagnat) on Crispy Garlic Bread

instructions.primary_message: Place eggs in a small saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes. Drain hot water and add ice or run under cold water to cool.
Place peas in colander and run under cold water to thaw. Transfer to a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry; set aside.
Place oil, vinegar, mayo, capers, and Dijon in a small bowl; whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
1 tbsp red wine vinegar
1 tbsp mayonnaise
½ tbsp capers
1 tsp Dijon mustard

instructions.primary_message: Drain tuna and add to the bowl with the dressing. Add peas, stir to combine, and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message: 1 (120 g) can chunk light tuna in water

instructions.primary_message: Wash, dry, and slice tomato into rounds; place in a medium bowl.
Wash, dry, and shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems. Add to the bowl with the tomatoes.
Drain and thinly slice artichokes. Halve olives and add both to the bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ (106 g) jar artichoke hearts, marinated
½ cup Kalamata olives, pitted

instructions.primary_message: Peel and thinly slice shallot into rings. Add to the bowl and toss to combine the sandwich topping; set aside.

Cut rolls in half and place, cut-side up, on a baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil, then sprinkle with minced garlic and Italian seasoning. Place in the oven and toast, until golden and slightly crisp, 4-5 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp Italian seasoning

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, peel and slice eggs into rounds.
Spoon tuna mixture over the toasted rolls; layer with sandwich topping and sliced eggs.
To serve, divide sandwiches between plates and enjoy!
